before: refine Label defines a scoped variation of Label methods inside a module. using Highlight activates it for subsequent code in the current lexical scope; here that scope is the remainder of this source file. using cannot be called inside a method body.

A method defined before activation does not inherit the caller’s refinements just because it is called afterward. earlier was defined without Highlight active. Refinements avoid a global class rewrite, but their lexical lookup must still be understood when code crosses files or method definitions.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
class Label
  def text
    "plain"
  end
end
module Highlight
  refine Label do
    def text
      "bright"
    end
  end
end
def earlier(item)
  item.text
end
using Highlight
puts Label.new.text
puts earlier(Label.new)
```

Expected output or behavior: bright
plain. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Calls written in the affected scope can use the bright version of text.

Follow the labeled parts of this example.
```ruby
class Label
  def text
    "plain"
  end
end
module Highlight
  refine Label do
    def text
      "bright"
    end
  end
end
def earlier(item)
  item.text
end
using Highlight
puts Label.new.text
puts earlier(Label.new)
```
The output is `bright`, then `plain`. The direct call uses bright. The earlier method was defined before activation and still uses plain.
